subject: CareLogic logging & PII follow-up: redaction runbook and pilot proposal
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@carelogic.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap and next steps — logging controls & PII handling (CareLogic)

Elena / CareLogic team — thanks again for taking time this morning. Short recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of asks from your side:
- Which request/response fields must be removed vs pseudonymized vs allowed in logs (headers, body snippets, cookies, Authorization).
- Data residency and retention expectations (HIPAA constraints + long-term archival requirements).
- Debuggability requirements: is reversible mapping needed for trace IDs or would a one-way pseudonym suffice?
- Evidence required for procurement: SOC 2 artifact, sample sanitized logs, and a playbook for incident debug.

Redwood proposal (high-level):
- Pre-ingest redaction rules in the Private/VPC offering to mask Authorization, Cookie, and any header/value keys you indicate. We can apply header allowlists and body scrubbing for PII patterns.
- Trace IDs: two options: (A) one-way HMAC(hash) with customer-specific salt (recommended for production) or (B) reversible tokenization when customer KMS is provided and strict access controls/audit logs are required.
- Retention: default short-term logs 30 days in active cluster, with optional archival to customer S3 for longer retention. For HIPAA workloads we recommend 30 day active + encrypted cold storage on customer account.
- Debug window: we can provide an ephemeral mapping store (encrypted, access-audited) for up to 7 days to enable debugging; after that only hashed values remain.

Pilot ask and deliverables:
- 2-week POC: Redwood will instrument the pre-ingest redaction rules, run 5% sampling of request/response traffic with your sample dataset, and deliver sanitized sample logs + a runbook describing the rules.
- Deliverables: redaction-runbook-v1.pdf, logging-matrix-carelogic.xlsx, and a short demo walkthrough.

Next steps (proposed):
1) CareLogic to confirm which headers and body fields must be removed vs hashed (see attached matrix).
2) Legal/InfoSec: share BAA requirement and any procurement checklist; we’ll surface the SOC 2 evidence.
3) Schedule pilot start window (we have capacity the weeks of Sep 27 or Oct 4).

Attaching: redaction-runbook-v1.pdf (draft), logging-matrix-carelogic.xlsx (fill-in matrix).

If helpful I can also map the proposed redaction to our runtime controls (pre-ingest, continuous batching path, KV cache masking) in a short doc.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and next steps — logging controls & PII handling (CareLogic)

Thanks Mina — that matches our notes. A few clarifying questions before we commit to a pilot: 

1) VPC/on-prem: can the pre-ingest redaction run entirely within our VPC so no raw request/response leaves our network? We prefer that model for PHI.
2) Trace ID handling: for operational debugging our SREs sometimes need to map a trace back to a session; reversible tokenization is preferred if it can be locked to our KMS and access requires explicit approval. Is that supported?
3) Retention: HIPAA requires us to have clear retention and deletion policies. Can you support deletion of logs on demand (legal hold exceptions aside)?
4) Procurement: we will need a BAA and SOC 2 Type II evidence. Legal will also ask about key rotation and HSM usage.

We can aim for a short pilot week starting Sep 27. Please provide a brief pilot SOW and rough cost estimate.

—Elena
Elena Torres
VP Security & Compliance, CareLogic Health
elena.torres@carelogic.com | +1 (617) 555-4422
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@carelogic.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and next steps — logging controls & PII handling (CareLogic)

Elena — quick answers inline and a proposed path forward.

1) VPC/on-prem: yes. For Redwood Private the pre-ingest path runs inside your VPC (customer-controlled network egress). No raw request/response needs to transit our hosted control plane during the scrubbing step; we can run the ingest agent in your environment and push only sanitized artifacts to our control plane if you prefer.

2) Reversible tokenization: supported via envelope encryption + customer KMS. Flow: incoming trace_id -> tokenization service (inside your VPC) -> token stored in an encrypted token vault; Redwood requires audit logging for every token unwrap. If you require the operation be reversible only by your ops, we can configure access so the unwrap requires a signed request by your key-holder. Important tradeoff: reversible mapping increases blast radius, so for production we recommend HMAC one-way mapping unless you have a strict debug use-case.

3) Deletion: we support on-demand deletion requests for logs stored on Redwood-managed storage; for Private deployments we can enact deletion policies and deletion APIs that operate against customer S3/archive buckets. Legal holds are supported (we won’t purge data covered under legal hold).

4) Procurement evidence: we’ll start the BAA loop with Legal; SOC 2 Type II artifact is available and we’ll share the most recent report under NDA. Key rotation/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for signing where required.

Pilot SOW (brief):
- Duration: 2 weeks (data collection + validation).
- Scope: implement header redaction rules per attached matrix, 5% sampling of request/response traffic, implement HMAC one-way mapping of trace_id with customer-provided salt (or reversible tokenization if you opt-in), deliver sanitized sample logs + runbook, 30 minute handoff call.
- Estimated cost: pilot (SaaS) $6k — applies as credit toward first-month Dedicated commitment if you convert.

If that sounds right we’ll: 1) generate a one-page SOW and send a calendar invite for Sep 27 kickoff; 2) loop our legal for the BAA; 3) you complete the attached matrix with the fields to redact/hash.

Best — Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
